LESSON: ROTE COUNTING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: THEME: MY FAMILY Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning
Topic 2.1: Rote Counting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rote Counting, part of THEME: MY FAMILY Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: How can you count numbers 1-10?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Rote count numbers 1-10, Learners with speech difficulties could use other alternative modes of communication to count numbers. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to- speech application/ point/sign/write) during the activity.

2. Team up with peers in purposive groups/pairs to rote count numbers 1-10 using actions (walk, clap, nod, tap, hop or stamp) as they mention family members, Learners with mobility difficulties could use relevant assistive devices. While those with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body to perform the given tasks.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Rote count numbers 1-10, Learners with speech difficulties could use other alternative modes of communication to count numbers. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to- speech application/ point/sign/write) during the activity.
2. Team up with peers in purposive groups/pairs to rote count numbers 1-10 using actions (walk, clap, nod, tap, hop or stamp) as they mention family members, Learners with mobility difficulties could use relevant assistive devices. While those with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body to perform the given tasks.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rote Counting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Self-efficacy: learners sing songs and recite poems on rote counting numbers 1-10 using actions.

Values:
Respect: learners take turns while rote counting numbers 1-10.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety: learners carefully do rote counting numbers 1-10 using actions.
